question: Should agent behavior governance become a new core security/config contract, or should this capability remain an optional plugin built on the existing typed hooks?
rationale: The choice determines the trusted security boundary, configuration compatibility contract, enforcement coverage, and whether OpenClaw maintains one policy system or two.

options.title: Move governance to a plugin
options.body: Use existing typed hooks and plugin-owned configuration, adding only narrowly proven generic hook gaps to core.

options.title: Sponsor a core contract
options.body: Approve a core design only after defining schema, all agent and delivery paths, failure semantics, migrations, docs, and live security proof.

options.title: Pause the proposal
options.body: Close or defer the PR if maintainers do not want to own a permanent behavior-governance security contract.

recommendation.title: Move governance to a plugin
recommendation.body: Use existing typed hooks and plugin-owned configuration, adding only narrowly proven generic hook gaps to core.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core agent prompts, plugin architecture, public config, and the repository security model.
